Control Tower Operating Model

The system converts factory signals into management decisions.

–Finance owns the truth of numbers.
–Operations owns the action plan.
CONTROLLING WORK
FIN 01

Margin Bridge

Explains plan-to-actual movement by price, mix, cost, volume, and exchange impact.

FIN 02

Cost Variance

Separates material, labor, overhead, scrap, and logistics variance for clear ownership.

FIN 03

Budget Guardrail

Flags spend above approved monthly run-rate before closing pressure starts.

FIN 04

Pricing Support

Links component cost movement to product margin and customer transfer pricing.

AUTOMATION SUPPORT
AUTO 01

Data Intake

Loads SAP exports, planning files, and quality logs into one reviewed working pack.

AUTO 02

Slide Drafting

Turns approved JSON data into consistent executive slides without manual formatting.

AUTO 03

Quality Gate

Blocks missing fields, crowding risk, broken templates, and unsafe presentation output.

4

Reporting Model Comparison

Same factory, different decision quality
Why the control tower changes the conversation
ERP Reports

Reliable transaction base, but fragmented by module and hard to read quickly.

Good for audit trail; weak for executive action without manual explanation.

Excel Pack

Flexible and familiar, but version control and late changes create risk.

Strong analyst tool; fragile as the final management product.

Control Tower

Connects KPI, owner, driver, action, and status into one management view.

Best for closing meetings where decisions must be clear and fast.

Control principle

ERP remains the source of truth.
The control tower becomes the source of management understanding.

Variance Drivers

Dummy root-cause structure for one monthly close

Material

  • –Compressor price increase from supplier reset.
  • –Higher resin usage after model mix change.
  • –Emergency freight for late imported parts.
  • –Purchase price variance not yet reflected in forecast.

Conversion

  • –Overtime used to recover two days of downtime.
  • –Line changeover loss increased on premium models.
  • –Utility cost above plan during heat wave.
  • –Maintenance spend pulled forward from next month.

Commercial Mix

  • –Export orders shifted toward lower-margin SKU.
  • –Local channel discount increased to clear stock.
  • –Spare-parts sales improved gross margin rate.
  • –Transfer price update delayed until next cycle.

Decision Requests

Dummy asks prepared for executive alignment

Approve

  • –Fast-track supplier renegotiation for cooling compressor.
  • –Lock July overtime ceiling before production recovery starts.
  • –Approve one owner for each high-impact variance line.

Challenge

  • –Review low-margin export mix before accepting extra volume.
  • –Question premium SKU launch timing if scrap does not improve.
  • –Reject manual slide changes after final close gate.

Monitor

  • –Track daily material burn rate against approved forecast.
  • –Update stock cover every morning for critical parts.
  • –Escalate margin bridge movement above $150K.
